content.thinking:
The fix shader would double-convert if applied without the palette-exact condition, so this needs to be gated on renderer type. I also notice the UPDATE_DISABLED resize case shows grey rather than black, which is a real behavioral difference worth flagging. I should wrap up findings now rather than making an advisor call given time constraints.

My key finding is that use_hdr_2d on a world SubViewport viewed through a container produces linear, unconverted colors instead of proper sRGB conversion — this conflicts with the "palette exact" requirement and the single-hook-ownership design. I'm weighing two fixes: either disable use_hdr_2d for the minimum viable product until a lighting need is proven, or make the container material a mandatory resolve shader owned separately from the Filter's slot, which would require restructuring the filter routing and guarding against double-conversion when the compatibility renderer ignores hdr_2d entirely.

I'm also flagging a second issue: the driver fallback defaulting to Compatibility mode silently on unsupported APIs undermines the release-build assumption that effective values are asserted and logged rather than silently degraded — I think this should become a non-blocking major issue, with explicit fallback flags required and possibly a fatal error on unexpected method rather than silent continuation.

Third, I'm confirming that frame_pre_draw fires after all _process calls on the main thread in the same frame, meaning anything reading pose data during _process is working with the previous frame's stale pose — this is a real engine-level timing fact that creates a one-frame lag incompatible with the HUD/world sync requirement, and I'm leaning toward marking it blocking.

Looking at ADR-0009's CAMERA_SOLVE stage, I see the design itself is self-contradictory: section 7.3 states PipelineRoot._process computes world_to_hud, but CameraSolver actually runs inside pre_draw — so the spec claims the solve happens during _process while the architecture places it afterward, which confirms this should be blocking since the ADR is still Proposed and explicitly says this must be resolved before acceptance.

Finally, I'm updating the UNVERIFIED claims around frame_pre_draw since they're now confirmed with high confidence, meaning the PRESENTATION_LATE fallback is unnecessary and this item is non-blocking.

E6: OQ-F resolved — root draw calls count the composite correctly (3 containers give root=3 across Forward+ and Compat), confirmed for both root and per-viewport counts; confidence high despite small sample.

E7: canvas layer ties at same index are broken by tree order, confirmed by probe (second sibling renders on top), likely because engine uses get_index() as sublayer order; caveat applies only to siblings under the same parent and breaks under reparenting/reorder. I'm recommending just using distinct layer values (3, 4, shifting debug to 5) to avoid relying on this behavior.

E8: probed that snap flags under pass B apply in override/base-px space, so the belt-and-braces approach holds there too.

Now I'm noting that ADR-0009's question about what snap flags snap to is actually answered by ADR-0008's spike, and confirming canvas_transform units under override stretch are base pixels (shift of -5 becomes 15 screen px). Snap rounds rather than floors, which doesn't matter for integer values — non-blocking.

E9: container with NEAREST scale 3 shows no edge bleed and an exact 24px span under Forward+ at 1280x720 with flat fill, partially resolving OQ-B for pass A; untested for non-flat textures, Compat, fractional positions, or release export — confidence medium, non-blocking, and container position must stay integer per the ADR.

E10: deciding to make render mode a constructor-injected enum argument to ViewportWiring rather than a hardcoded build constant, since GDScript consts can't be overridden for branching between the two wiring paths.

I'm checking whether using a const in a conditional branch would trigger any GDScript warnings under ADR-0010's strict warnings-as-errors policy — concluding there's likely no such warning (no "constant condition" warning exists in GDScript), so I'll just note this as a possible concern rather than a hard claim.

E11: there's a process-order conflict — PipelineRoot ties with presentation nodes at PRESENTATION priority and needs tree-order tie-breaking, but ADR-0008 says subscribers draw from their own _process at PRESENTATION while ADR-0009 says presenters define no _process, which only resolves if PipelineRoot itself is the PresentationHost calling its own derive before the driver's frame.

E12: the zoom cooldown timer scales with Engine.time_scale, but whether ADR-0001 actually sets time_scale is unverified — this seems low priority enough to possibly leave out of the tight list.

E13: checking the Windows driver default claim — that a project without an explicit rendering key reports Vulkan as default — versus whether D3D12 is truly the Windows default only for newer project templates, which remains unverified; the ADR's approach of pinning the effective value rather than assuming defaults seems like the right call here.

The editor drops keys that match default values on save, so there's no way to force an explicit key — the effective-value assertion is correct as-is. I'm checking E14 next: whether the 4.7 typed-return override rules, const usage, packed arrays, and class naming could clash with engine internals — compiling the interface snippets against 4.7.2 shows no violations, none of the 24 class names collide with engine classes, and I'm now looking at whether a packed array parameter passed into a supposedly "pure" function could actually be mutated by the caller.

Caller mutation would be visible if the reference is retained, so the fix is to duplicate or copy the array rather than pass it directly; I'm also noting the warnings-as-errors policy means a setting lookup returning a generic Variant needs explicit typed casts, which is non-blocking but worth flagging. I'll split this into E14 (no real compile issues, informational) and E15 (the packed array reference plus a signature mismatch between one-arg and two-arg versions of a function, flagged as an inconsistency). Then I move to E17, the Windows modal resize loop behavior, which I can't verify and mark as low-confidence, and E18, the shader baker requiring matching drivers in the export preset, which I'll include briefly as a low-confidence gotcha.

Then I work through E19, checking whether fractional HUD sizing under a layer scale causes non-integer pixel edges, and conclude it actually resolves cleanly to integer screen pixels so there's no real issue there. The more substantive gotcha I land on is that text rendered under a scaled CanvasLayer could look blurry unless nearest-neighbor filtering is applied, and since CanvasLayer itself isn't a CanvasItem, I need to rely on the viewport's default texture filter setting instead.

I'm also uncertain whether dynamic fonts under a scaled canvas get rasterized at the right resolution — Godot 4.5's oversampling feature might address this, but I'd flag this as a low-confidence gotcha rather than something I'm sure about, and I decide to skip the transparent background/HDR clear color edge case and note that glow effects require a WorldEnvironment with proper canvas mode inside the SubViewport.

Now I'm working through the cross-ADR conflicts: one issue is that camera solve location is ambiguous between ADR-0008 and ADR-0009, so I'm proposing to move the solve step into ADR-0009's pipeline stage and have pre_draw just write the already-resolved transform. Another is that it's unclear whether subscribers run their own process or go through a single PresentationHost, so I want ADR-0008 to explicitly declare PipelineRoot as that host. A third is that the PRESENTATION_LATE process priority request seems unnecessary now that frame_pre_draw ordering is verified, so I'm leaning toward withdrawing that open question as low severity.

I'm also noting that the snap-flag behavior under SubViewport variants needs ADR-0009 to document what ADR-0008 already resolved experimentally, and that ADR-0010's PRJ-02 list of stretch pins and project.godot keys needs to either carry or reference ADR-0008's fuller key list, plus flag the warnings-as-errors interaction with Variant casts in the render config reader as a minor issue. The kernel state accessor and DisplaySettings float questions don't apply here, so I'm skipping those, and I'm flagging that ADR-0008's canvas_transform being a Transform2D raises a float32 exactness question tied to ADR-0005.

With the open items worked through, I'm settling on a blocking verdict driven by E1 and E3, and now I'll write up the final output using high/medium/low severity labels, keeping it concise but complete.

findings.text: The world SubViewport with use_hdr_2d=true, drawn through a SubViewportContainer onto the SDR root, outputs unconverted linear colour. Windowed probe on 4.7.2 Forward+ (Vulkan, NVIDIA): a flat Color8(128,64,200) fill reads back as (55,13,147) from the HDR viewport and as (128,64,200) from an SDR viewport. Clear-colour pixels also came out as (19,19,19) instead of 76. The engine only converts linear to sRGB when the viewport is attached to the screen. So use_hdr_2d=true on the world viewport (S2.2, S5.1) contradicts the ADR's own container-material-null-at-MVP rule (S2.4), the 'filter_route=PER_ELEMENT, slot=NOT_USED' state, the 'palette-exact fills' goal, and the 'SDR-exact' statement for the root. Probed fix: a container ShaderMaterial doing exact linear-to-sRGB (mix(pow(c,1/2.4)*1.055-0.055, c*12.92, c<=0.0031308)) restores (128,64,200) exactly under Forward+. That fix is renderer-specific. Under --rendering-method gl_compatibility, use_hdr_2d is silently ignored, so the plain viewport is exact and the same shader double-converts to (188,137,229). Confidence: high (probed both renderers). The ADR's 'use_hdr_2d is Forward+/Mobile only' training-knowledge claim is also confirmed: Compatibility ignores it. Values above 1.0 clamp at the container draw unless the resolve shader tonemaps them.
findings.amendment: Pick one and write it into S2.2/S2.4/S5.1. (a) MVP default use_hdr_2d=false on the world viewport until lighting spike steps 7 and 8 prove it is needed. Keep the container material null and keep the flat-palette guarantee. (b) If HDR is kept, add a mandatory PipelineRoot-owned 'resolve' material (linear-to-sRGB plus a clamp or tonemap policy) on the container. Define how it composes with the Filter's slot: either the Filter shader includes the resolve, or a second full-screen stage is added. Gate it on the effective rendering method: no resolve under Compatibility. Then D_filter becomes 1 (not 0) and filter_route/slot are no longer NOT_USED. Either way, add a StartupCheck row and a windowed palette read-back test (flat fill in, same fill out, per renderer). Record the probe numbers in Engine Compatibility.

findings.text: The camera solve placement is self-contradictory. S6.2 and S7.3 put CameraSolver.solve inside the RenderingServer.frame_pre_draw handler. S7.3 and the diagram have PipelineRoot._process compute world_to_hud for 32 prompts and have subscribers draw from read views. Probed 4.7.2 windowed: frame_pre_draw fires on the main thread after every _process of the frame, including priority 1000, and before the draw. This held under both thread_model 1 and 2. A canvas_transform written there is the one drawn that same frame (marker x equalled the value written in the handler). A write from _process is also drawn that same frame. So anything that reads pose_q or world_to_hud during _process (HUD prompts, the Avatar presenter's beam pose, mouse_to_world_aim) sees the previous frame's pose while the world draws the new one. That is a permanent one-frame HUD-versus-world disagreement, on exactly the 'screen is still when the ship is still' surface. Confidence: high (probed).
findings.amendment: Run CameraSolver.solve in the _process pass at the CAMERA_SOLVE stage (ADR-0009 stage 1), before HUD, Lighting and Avatar. Publish pose_q and the jolt offset to the camera host. The frame_pre_draw handler then does only the two writes (WorldViewport.canvas_transform, parallax offsets) from the already-solved values. It does not solve, and it is idempotent and branch-free. Update S6.1/S6.2, the diagram, the S7.3 row 'CameraSolver.solve (inside the frame_pre_draw handler)', and PR-6 C2. This also removes any dependency on the unprobable-headless signal for solver logic, so the solver stays unit-testable.

findings.text: The UNVERIFIED frame_pre_draw claims in S6.2 and Verification Required (2) are now resolved by probe. It fires after all _process calls and before draw, on the main thread (thread_model 1 and 2). A direct Viewport.canvas_transform write there is drawn that frame. It only fires when a frame is actually drawn (never headless, which the ADR already notes). Not tested: a release export, window minimised or occluded, and low-processor mode. The PRESENTATION_LATE fallback and the OQ-D request to amend ADR-0001 are unnecessary. Confidence: high for dev-build Windows Forward+ on one GPU; medium for release export.
findings.amendment: Replace the UNVERIFIED text with the probe result. Withdraw OQ-D and the PRESENTATION_LATE request. Keep a release-export re-run of the same probe in spike step 12. Add 'the write must be idempotent and safe if the handler is skipped for a frame (minimised window)'.

findings.text: S2.2 and OQ-G assume UPDATE_DISABLED holds the last texture across a resize. Probed: resizing a SubViewport while render_target_update_mode=UPDATE_DISABLED blanks it. Forward+ gives (0,0,0) in the container. Compatibility shows the clear colour. Setting UPDATE_ONCE then redraws it, and it is composited in the same frame, so the planned UPDATE_ONCE guard is both required and sufficient. After the one-shot, the node's render_target_update_mode property still reads UPDATE_ONCE (the engine does not write it back), so PipelineRoot must set UPDATE_DISABLED itself. Re-assigning UPDATE_ONCE on a later resize worked. Not tested: whether a disabled viewport holds its texture without a resize (the PAUSED_FROZEN hold). Confidence: high for resize behaviour; PAUSED_FROZEN no-resize hold UNVERIFIED but likely.
findings.amendment: State in S2.2/S3.2 that any size change while disabled clears the target, so UPDATE_ONCE on that frame is mandatory, not a guard. Track the desired mode in ViewportWiring instead of reading the property back. Add a step-11 check: pause, resize the window, confirm there is no black frame. Add a second check: pause with no resize, confirm the frame is held.

findings.text: S1/S5 let a release build 'log and continue' on a wrong effective driver or method. The engine has rendering/rendering_device/fallback_to_opengl3 (default true; probed present) and fallback_to_d3d12 and fallback_to_vulkan (both default true). If Vulkan init fails on a user's machine, the engine silently falls back (to D3D12, and ultimately to OpenGL3 Compatibility). In Compatibility, use_hdr_2d is ignored, Light2D and glow behave differently, and (per E1) the colour path changes. The release build would then ship a different look with only a diagnostics-header line. Confidence: high that the keys exist and default to true; the silent fallback sequence itself is not probed.
findings.amendment: Add to the S5.1 table as required keys in project.godot: fallback_to_opengl3=false, and fallback_to_d3d12=false while Vulkan is the pin (fallback_to_vulkan=false if the D3D12 reversal is taken). A failed driver init then errors visibly instead of degrading silently. Make the release-build response to a method mismatch a visible fatal 'unsupported GPU' screen, or at least a user-facing notice, not a header log line.

findings.text: OQ-C and the 'probed 2026-10-28' claims. Windowed 4.7.2: a project with no driver key reports driver=vulkan / forward_plus. ProjectSettings default for rendering_device/driver.windows is vulkan, linuxbsd is vulkan, macos is metal. The reference's 'D3D12 is the Windows default since 4.6' is therefore not what a key-absent project gets; it is most plausibly a new-project-template value (UNVERIFIED, not probed). The ADR's effective-value assertion handles both cases and is the right approach. Also confirmed present with the stated defaults: display/window/hdr/request_hdr_output=false, per_pixel_transparency/allowed=false, use_debanding=false, hdr_2d=false, scale_mode=fractional, allow_hidpi=true, snap_controls_to_pixels=true, low_processor_mode=false, vsync_mode=1, default_texture_filter=1, snap_2d_*=false, default_clear_color=(0.3,0.3,0.3,1). The SubViewport/SubViewportContainer defaults I re-ran are plausible and match. One caveat: all of these headless probes ran under Compatibility, as the ADR itself says, and only the project-setting defaults are renderer-independent. Confidence: high.
findings.amendment: Edit OQ-C to record that a project with no key gets vulkan on 4.7.2 (windowed probe) and that the D3D12 default is probably a template write. Suggest correcting docs/engine-reference/godot/modules/rendering.md and breaking-changes.md accordingly. Do not claim more than this without opening the project-creation flow.

findings.text: Two CanvasLayers at the same layer index: probed, the later sibling (green) draws over the earlier (red). This is consistent with the engine passing the node's sibling index as the sublayer stacking key. This resolves the 'tree order UNVERIFIED' part of S2.5/OQ-G for siblings under one parent. It is fragile to reparenting or reordering. Confidence: high for same-parent siblings; not tested across different parents.
findings.amendment: Cheapest and robust: give MenuReadingLayer its own index (pixel face 3, reading face 4, debug 5) and drop the shared-index dependency. If the shared index is kept, record the sibling-index tie-break as probed, require both layers under PipelineRoot in a fixed order, and add a boot-walk assertion on their get_index() order.

findings.text: Answers to ADR-0009 questions about the snap flags and units under pass B (probed on a 600x12 viewport, override 200x4, stretch true, snap_2d_transforms_to_pixel=true). canvas_transform is in override (base-pixel) units: an x offset of -5 moved content by 15 screen px. Snapping happens in base-pixel space: a node at 10.4 with offset -5 gives 5.4, which snaps to 5, drawn at screen x=15. So the 'belt and braces' flags do snap to base pixels, not screen pixels, under pass B. They round to nearest rather than floor, which does not matter when placement is integer. Confidence: medium (single probe, Forward+).
findings.amendment: Record the result in S2.2/S4 and tell ADR-0009 that the snap flags snap to base px in both passes. Keep 'nothing relies on them'. Note that pose_q and parallax offsets must still be written as integer-valued Vector2 so rounding versus floor never differs.

findings.text: OQ-B/Verification (6), partial: a SubViewportContainer with stretch=false, scale=(3,3) and texture_filter=NEAREST drew an 8x4 viewport as exactly 24x12 screen px with a flat fill, with no bleed on either side and exact colour (SDR viewport). The width was exactly 24 px (x=700..723). Not tested: textured or non-flat content, fractional container position, Compatibility, pass B, release export. Confidence: medium for pass A flat content only.
findings.amendment: Keep step 11, but narrow it to the untested combinations: a textured sheet, a one-pixel checker, pass B, and an odd window size. Record the flat-fill probe as already passing.

findings.text: Draw-call accounting (OQ-F), probed in Forward+ and Compatibility. Viewport.get_render_info(RENDER_INFO_TYPE_CANVAS, RENDER_INFO_DRAW_CALLS_IN_FRAME) works per viewport. A root with only three SubViewportContainers reported 3 canvas draw calls, so the container composite IS counted on the root (one call per container). The sub-viewport's own count was separate (1 for one ColorRect). The signature and enum names in S7 are correct. So D_root closed is 63, not 62, in the ADR's own arithmetic (60 + 1 hold + 1 filter + 1 composite), and the chart-open figure 92 rises to 93 unless D_L3 is lowered. Confidence: medium-high (small scene).
findings.amendment: Add an explicit 'container composite' row (1 call, root) to S7.1 and fix D_root (63 and 93, or re-derive the caps). Resolve OQ-F from this probe and re-run in the release export. Add a note that DRAW_CALLS_IN_FRAME is read after the frame, so it lags one frame when read in _process.

findings.text: API, compile and typing review found nothing that fails on 4.7.2. I wrote the Key Interfaces into a scratch project and compiled them headless: RenderLayout (static derive returning its own class, Vector2i/PackedInt32Array), PipelineRoot read-only properties with get-only accessors (layout, present_time), and StartupCheck.run returning Array[StartupFinding]. All 24 class_names in the ADR (DisplaySettings, RenderLayout, ViewportWiring, PipelineRoot, CameraSolver, Pose, SolverInput and so on) do not collide with engine classes (ClassDB.class_exists false for all). layout, version and present_time are not Node or Object properties or methods. There is no const of a constructed object (the constants are ints, floats or a table). The 4.7 typed-return override rule is not triggered, since the only override is _process (void). The packed-array setter change (4.7) is not touched. Minor issues: (a) offered_h: PackedInt32Array is passed by reference in a 'pure/immutable' derive. A caller that mutates it after the call, or a layout that keeps it, changes the result. (b) S3.3 gives world_to_hud(body_pos) with one argument while Key Interfaces gives (body_pos, pose_q). (c) 'immutable value' RenderLayout declares a mutable var version. (d) With ADR-0010's all-warnings-as-errors, RenderConfigReader must cast every ProjectSettings.get_setting() Variant, because inferred or unsafe declarations are errors. Confidence: high for compile result; medium for (d).
findings.amendment: Copy or duplicate() offered_h on entry, or take Array[int]. Make the world_to_hud signature one way (the two-argument form) in S3.3. Move version out of the value (PipelineRoot holds the counter) or drop the 'immutable' claim. Add a one-line note that the reader uses explicit typed casts.

findings.text: S4 says RENDER_MODE is 'a single build constant' read only by ViewportWiring, but Validation Criteria and Equivalence require 'a test constructs both wirings from the same input trace'. A GDScript const cannot be varied in a test.
findings.amendment: Make the mode a constructor argument of ViewportWiring (enum Mode {A, B}); the composition root passes a default from one const or feature tag. The equivalence test then constructs both. Keep the 'only ViewportWiring branches on it' lint.

findings.text: Engine gotchas the draft does not mention. (1) The zoom cooldown uses _process delta, which is scaled by Engine.time_scale; the ADR says 'engine process time'. ADR-0001 leaves time_scale scaling UNVERIFIED, so the cooldown is only 'wall-clock' if time_scale stays 1. (2) A Control with a non-Control parent (WorldContainer under a plain Node) lays out against the window, and the container's Control.size is only refreshed from the viewport's minimum size at the next deferred update. The probe shows drawing is unaffected with stretch=false, but any code that reads WorldContainer.size or mouse rects right after a resize sees stale values; only scale and position should be read. (3) Dynamic-font Labels and RichText under CanvasLayer.scale=H are rasterised at font size and then upscaled (blurry, not pixel-snapped) unless a bitmap face or font oversampling is configured; the ADR covers reading face at scale 1 but not HUD text faces. Confidence: medium on (1), (2); low on (3), which is not probed. (4) On Windows the main loop is driven from a timer during the modal edge-drag resize loop (recalled, not verified), which the step-11 2 s drag should cover. (5) Shader Baker only bakes for the drivers enabled in the export preset, so the preset must include Vulkan; it is not supported under Compatibility (recalled).
findings.amendment: Add a Gotchas list to Implementation Guidelines. Zoom cooldown: use delta divided by Engine.time_scale, or state that time_scale is always 1. Add a step-11 line for HUD text sharpness at H=3. Add a step-11 line for edge-drag cadence. Name the required drivers in the export preset checklist.

findings.text: canvas_transform is a Transform2D, which is float32 in the standard build. Integer-valued origins are exact only below 2^24 (16,777,216) base px. ADR-0005/0010 already list 'float32 canvas exactness' as an unverified assumption owned partly by ADR-0008. The camera solver holds float64 scalars, so the conversion to the float32 origin is the point where exactness is lost or kept. Confidence: medium (not probed here; Engine.is_double_precision() was not checked).
findings.amendment: State the exactness bound next to the camera write: pose_q is Vector2i, converted at the write, and body-frame coordinates are rebased so they stay inside the bound (the rebase mechanism already exists). Add a unit test at the bound. Resolve the ADR-0005/0010 'float32 canvas exactness' reference by citing this section.

cross_adr.text: Camera solve location conflict (ADR-0009 OQ-J). ADR-0008 solves in frame_pre_draw. ADR-0009 solves at CAMERA_SOLVE stage 1 in the driver's _process because the HUD (stage 5) needs world_to_hud. The 4.7.2 probe shows frame_pre_draw fires after all _process, so a solve there is invisible to _process readers for a frame (see E2). ADR-0009's position is the one that works on this engine.
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0008 S6.1/S6.2/S7.3 and the diagram: move CameraSolver.solve into the CAMERA_SOLVE stage. The frame_pre_draw handler only writes canvas_transform and parallax offsets from the solved pose. ADR-0009 needs no change beyond citing the probed ordering.

cross_adr.text: Presenter execution model and priority label. ADR-0008 (S6.2 scope edge and diagram) says subscribers draw from their own _process at priority 0. ADR-0009 says presenters define no _process and a single PresentationHost, which may be the Pipeline root, calls a PresentationDriver at ProcessPriority.PRESENTATION (OQ-L). PipelineRoot at the same priority as subscribers would tie on tree order, which ADR-0001 refuses to rely on.
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0008 declares PipelineRoot to be the PresentationHost (ADR-0009 asks ADR-0008 to decide). Its single _process first does present_time, the zoom cooldown and the RESCALING re-derive, then calls driver.frame(). Replace the literal '0' in the diagram with ProcessPriority.PRESENTATION. No new ADR-0001 constant is needed.

cross_adr.text: OQ-D asks ADR-0001 for an additive PRESENTATION_LATE constant as the fallback camera-write point. With frame_pre_draw probed as working (E3) and the solve moved (X1), the request is unnecessary.
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0008 withdraws OQ-D. ADR-0001 stays at three constants. Re-check in the release-export probe.

cross_adr.text: ADR-0009 (snap-flag lines near 264 and 377) defers 'what the snap flags snap to under the SubViewport variants' to ADR-0008. Probe: they snap to base-pixel space under pass B, and canvas_transform is in base-pixel units (E8).
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0008 records the probe result in S2.2/S4. ADR-0009 cites it and may drop the 'unknown' wording.

cross_adr.text: ADR-0010 PRJ-02 delegates the stretch pins to ADR-0008, but ADR-0008 S5.1 adds more required project.godot keys: scale_mode=integer, window overrides, default_texture_filter=0, snap_2d_*, clear colour, and (per E5) the fallback_to_* keys. ADR-0010's warnings-as-errors policy also forces typed casts on ProjectSettings reads in RenderConfigReader.
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0010 PRJ-02 references ADR-0008 S5.1 as the normative key list (including the fallback_to_* keys once added). The RenderConfigReader lint exemption or cast pattern is stated once there.

cross_adr.text: ADR-0005 and ADR-0010 both cite 'float32 canvas exactness' as an assumption owned partly by ADR-0008, which ADR-0008 does not address (E14).
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0008 adds the 2^24 integer-exactness bound and the Vector2i-to-float32 conversion point at the canvas_transform write; ADR-0005/0010 then cite it.

findings.text: The world SubViewport with use_hdr_2d=true, drawn through a SubViewportContainer onto the SDR root, outputs unconverted linear colour. Windowed probe on 4.7.2 Forward+ (Vulkan, NVIDIA): a flat Color8(128,64,200) fill reads back as (55,13,147) from the HDR viewport and as (128,64,200) from an SDR viewport. Clear-colour pixels also came out as (19,19,19) instead of 76. The engine only converts linear to sRGB when the viewport is attached to the screen. So use_hdr_2d=true on the world viewport (S2.2, S5.1) contradicts the ADR's own container-material-null-at-MVP rule (S2.4), the 'filter_route=PER_ELEMENT, slot=NOT_USED' state, the 'palette-exact fills' goal, and the 'SDR-exact' statement for the root. Probed fix: a container ShaderMaterial doing exact linear-to-sRGB (mix(pow(c,1/2.4)*1.055-0.055, c*12.92, c<=0.0031308)) restores (128,64,200) exactly under Forward+. That fix is renderer-specific. Under --rendering-method gl_compatibility, use_hdr_2d is silently ignored, so the plain viewport is exact and the same shader double-converts to (188,137,229). Confidence: high (probed both renderers). The ADR's 'use_hdr_2d is Forward+/Mobile only' training-knowledge claim is also confirmed: Compatibility ignores it. Values above 1.0 clamp at the container draw unless the resolve shader tonemaps them.
findings.amendment: Pick one and write it into S2.2/S2.4/S5.1. (a) MVP default use_hdr_2d=false on the world viewport until lighting spike steps 7 and 8 prove it is needed. Keep the container material null and keep the flat-palette guarantee. (b) If HDR is kept, add a mandatory PipelineRoot-owned 'resolve' material (linear-to-sRGB plus a clamp or tonemap policy) on the container. Define how it composes with the Filter's slot: either the Filter shader includes the resolve, or a second full-screen stage is added. Gate it on the effective rendering method: no resolve under Compatibility. Then D_filter becomes 1 (not 0) and filter_route/slot are no longer NOT_USED. Either way, add a StartupCheck row and a windowed palette read-back test (flat fill in, same fill out, per renderer). Record the probe numbers in Engine Compatibility.

findings.text: The camera solve placement is self-contradictory. S6.2 and S7.3 put CameraSolver.solve inside the RenderingServer.frame_pre_draw handler. S7.3 and the diagram have PipelineRoot._process compute world_to_hud for 32 prompts and have subscribers draw from read views. Probed 4.7.2 windowed: frame_pre_draw fires on the main thread after every _process of the frame, including priority 1000, and before the draw. This held under both thread_model 1 and 2. A canvas_transform written there is the one drawn that same frame (marker x equalled the value written in the handler). A write from _process is also drawn that same frame. So anything that reads pose_q or world_to_hud during _process (HUD prompts, the Avatar presenter's beam pose, mouse_to_world_aim) sees the previous frame's pose while the world draws the new one. That is a permanent one-frame HUD-versus-world disagreement, on exactly the 'screen is still when the ship is still' surface. Confidence: high (probed).
findings.amendment: Run CameraSolver.solve in the _process pass at the CAMERA_SOLVE stage (ADR-0009 stage 1), before HUD, Lighting and Avatar. Publish pose_q and the jolt offset to the camera host. The frame_pre_draw handler then does only the two writes (WorldViewport.canvas_transform, parallax offsets) from the already-solved values. It does not solve, and it is idempotent and branch-free. Update S6.1/S6.2, the diagram, the S7.3 row 'CameraSolver.solve (inside the frame_pre_draw handler)', and PR-6 C2. This also removes any dependency on the unprobable-headless signal for solver logic, so the solver stays unit-testable.

findings.text: The UNVERIFIED frame_pre_draw claims in S6.2 and Verification Required (2) are now resolved by probe. It fires after all _process calls and before draw, on the main thread (thread_model 1 and 2). A direct Viewport.canvas_transform write there is drawn that frame. It only fires when a frame is actually drawn (never headless, which the ADR already notes). Not tested: a release export, window minimised or occluded, and low-processor mode. The PRESENTATION_LATE fallback and the OQ-D request to amend ADR-0001 are unnecessary. Confidence: high for dev-build Windows Forward+ on one GPU; medium for release export.
findings.amendment: Replace the UNVERIFIED text with the probe result. Withdraw OQ-D and the PRESENTATION_LATE request. Keep a release-export re-run of the same probe in spike step 12. Add 'the write must be idempotent and safe if the handler is skipped for a frame (minimised window)'.

findings.text: S2.2 and OQ-G assume UPDATE_DISABLED holds the last texture across a resize. Probed: resizing a SubViewport while render_target_update_mode=UPDATE_DISABLED blanks it. Forward+ gives (0,0,0) in the container. Compatibility shows the clear colour. Setting UPDATE_ONCE then redraws it, and it is composited in the same frame, so the planned UPDATE_ONCE guard is both required and sufficient. After the one-shot, the node's render_target_update_mode property still reads UPDATE_ONCE (the engine does not write it back), so PipelineRoot must set UPDATE_DISABLED itself. Re-assigning UPDATE_ONCE on a later resize worked. Not tested: whether a disabled viewport holds its texture without a resize (the PAUSED_FROZEN hold). Confidence: high for resize behaviour; PAUSED_FROZEN no-resize hold UNVERIFIED but likely.
findings.amendment: State in S2.2/S3.2 that any size change while disabled clears the target, so UPDATE_ONCE on that frame is mandatory, not a guard. Track the desired mode in ViewportWiring instead of reading the property back. Add a step-11 check: pause, resize the window, confirm there is no black frame. Add a second check: pause with no resize, confirm the frame is held.

findings.text: S1/S5 let a release build 'log and continue' on a wrong effective driver or method. The engine has rendering/rendering_device/fallback_to_opengl3 (default true; probed present) and fallback_to_d3d12 and fallback_to_vulkan (both default true). If Vulkan init fails on a user's machine, the engine silently falls back (to D3D12, and ultimately to OpenGL3 Compatibility). In Compatibility, use_hdr_2d is ignored, Light2D and glow behave differently, and (per E1) the colour path changes. The release build would then ship a different look with only a diagnostics-header line. Confidence: high that the keys exist and default to true; the silent fallback sequence itself is not probed.
findings.amendment: Add to the S5.1 table as required keys in project.godot: fallback_to_opengl3=false, and fallback_to_d3d12=false while Vulkan is the pin (fallback_to_vulkan=false if the D3D12 reversal is taken). A failed driver init then errors visibly instead of degrading silently. Make the release-build response to a method mismatch a visible fatal 'unsupported GPU' screen, or at least a user-facing notice, not a header log line.

findings.text: OQ-C and the 'probed 2026-10-28' claims. Windowed 4.7.2: a project with no driver key reports driver=vulkan / forward_plus. ProjectSettings default for rendering_device/driver.windows is vulkan, linuxbsd is vulkan, macos is metal. The reference's 'D3D12 is the Windows default since 4.6' is therefore not what a key-absent project gets; it is most plausibly a new-project-template value (UNVERIFIED, not probed). The ADR's effective-value assertion handles both cases and is the right approach. Also confirmed present with the stated defaults: display/window/hdr/request_hdr_output=false, per_pixel_transparency/allowed=false, use_debanding=false, hdr_2d=false, scale_mode=fractional, allow_hidpi=true, snap_controls_to_pixels=true, low_processor_mode=false, vsync_mode=1, default_texture_filter=1, snap_2d_*=false, default_clear_color=(0.3,0.3,0.3,1). The SubViewport/SubViewportContainer defaults I re-ran are plausible and match. One caveat: all of these headless probes ran under Compatibility, as the ADR itself says, and only the project-setting defaults are renderer-independent. Confidence: high.
findings.amendment: Edit OQ-C to record that a project with no key gets vulkan on 4.7.2 (windowed probe) and that the D3D12 default is probably a template write. Suggest correcting docs/engine-reference/godot/modules/rendering.md and breaking-changes.md accordingly. Do not claim more than this without opening the project-creation flow.

findings.text: Two CanvasLayers at the same layer index: probed, the later sibling (green) draws over the earlier (red). This is consistent with the engine passing the node's sibling index as the sublayer stacking key. This resolves the 'tree order UNVERIFIED' part of S2.5/OQ-G for siblings under one parent. It is fragile to reparenting or reordering. Confidence: high for same-parent siblings; not tested across different parents.
findings.amendment: Cheapest and robust: give MenuReadingLayer its own index (pixel face 3, reading face 4, debug 5) and drop the shared-index dependency. If the shared index is kept, record the sibling-index tie-break as probed, require both layers under PipelineRoot in a fixed order, and add a boot-walk assertion on their get_index() order.

findings.text: Answers to ADR-0009 questions about the snap flags and units under pass B (probed on a 600x12 viewport, override 200x4, stretch true, snap_2d_transforms_to_pixel=true). canvas_transform is in override (base-pixel) units: an x offset of -5 moved content by 15 screen px. Snapping happens in base-pixel space: a node at 10.4 with offset -5 gives 5.4, which snaps to 5, drawn at screen x=15. So the 'belt and braces' flags do snap to base pixels, not screen pixels, under pass B. They round to nearest rather than floor, which does not matter when placement is integer. Confidence: medium (single probe, Forward+).
findings.amendment: Record the result in S2.2/S4 and tell ADR-0009 that the snap flags snap to base px in both passes. Keep 'nothing relies on them'. Note that pose_q and parallax offsets must still be written as integer-valued Vector2 so rounding versus floor never differs.

findings.text: OQ-B/Verification (6), partial: a SubViewportContainer with stretch=false, scale=(3,3) and texture_filter=NEAREST drew an 8x4 viewport as exactly 24x12 screen px with a flat fill, with no bleed on either side and exact colour (SDR viewport). The width was exactly 24 px (x=700..723). Not tested: textured or non-flat content, fractional container position, Compatibility, pass B, release export. Confidence: medium for pass A flat content only.
findings.amendment: Keep step 11, but narrow it to the untested combinations: a textured sheet, a one-pixel checker, pass B, and an odd window size. Record the flat-fill probe as already passing.

findings.text: Draw-call accounting (OQ-F), probed in Forward+ and Compatibility. Viewport.get_render_info(RENDER_INFO_TYPE_CANVAS, RENDER_INFO_DRAW_CALLS_IN_FRAME) works per viewport. A root with only three SubViewportContainers reported 3 canvas draw calls, so the container composite IS counted on the root (one call per container). The sub-viewport's own count was separate (1 for one ColorRect). The signature and enum names in S7 are correct. So D_root closed is 63, not 62, in the ADR's own arithmetic (60 + 1 hold + 1 filter + 1 composite), and the chart-open figure 92 rises to 93 unless D_L3 is lowered. Confidence: medium-high (small scene).
findings.amendment: Add an explicit 'container composite' row (1 call, root) to S7.1 and fix D_root (63 and 93, or re-derive the caps). Resolve OQ-F from this probe and re-run in the release export. Add a note that DRAW_CALLS_IN_FRAME is read after the frame, so it lags one frame when read in _process.

findings.text: API, compile and typing review found nothing that fails on 4.7.2. I wrote the Key Interfaces into a scratch project and compiled them headless: RenderLayout (static derive returning its own class, Vector2i/PackedInt32Array), PipelineRoot read-only properties with get-only accessors (layout, present_time), and StartupCheck.run returning Array[StartupFinding]. All 24 class_names in the ADR (DisplaySettings, RenderLayout, ViewportWiring, PipelineRoot, CameraSolver, Pose, SolverInput and so on) do not collide with engine classes (ClassDB.class_exists false for all). layout, version and present_time are not Node or Object properties or methods. There is no const of a constructed object (the constants are ints, floats or a table). The 4.7 typed-return override rule is not triggered, since the only override is _process (void). The packed-array setter change (4.7) is not touched. Minor issues: (a) offered_h: PackedInt32Array is passed by reference in a 'pure/immutable' derive. A caller that mutates it after the call, or a layout that keeps it, changes the result. (b) S3.3 gives world_to_hud(body_pos) with one argument while Key Interfaces gives (body_pos, pose_q). (c) 'immutable value' RenderLayout declares a mutable var version. (d) With ADR-0010's all-warnings-as-errors, RenderConfigReader must cast every ProjectSettings.get_setting() Variant, because inferred or unsafe declarations are errors. Confidence: high for compile result; medium for (d).
findings.amendment: Copy or duplicate() offered_h on entry, or take Array[int]. Make the world_to_hud signature one way (the two-argument form) in S3.3. Move version out of the value (PipelineRoot holds the counter) or drop the 'immutable' claim. Add a one-line note that the reader uses explicit typed casts.

findings.text: S4 says RENDER_MODE is 'a single build constant' read only by ViewportWiring, but Validation Criteria and Equivalence require 'a test constructs both wirings from the same input trace'. A GDScript const cannot be varied in a test.
findings.amendment: Make the mode a constructor argument of ViewportWiring (enum Mode {A, B}); the composition root passes a default from one const or feature tag. The equivalence test then constructs both. Keep the 'only ViewportWiring branches on it' lint.

findings.text: Engine gotchas the draft does not mention. (1) The zoom cooldown uses _process delta, which is scaled by Engine.time_scale; the ADR says 'engine process time'. ADR-0001 leaves time_scale scaling UNVERIFIED, so the cooldown is only 'wall-clock' if time_scale stays 1. (2) A Control with a non-Control parent (WorldContainer under a plain Node) lays out against the window, and the container's Control.size is only refreshed from the viewport's minimum size at the next deferred update. The probe shows drawing is unaffected with stretch=false, but any code that reads WorldContainer.size or mouse rects right after a resize sees stale values; only scale and position should be read. (3) Dynamic-font Labels and RichText under CanvasLayer.scale=H are rasterised at font size and then upscaled (blurry, not pixel-snapped) unless a bitmap face or font oversampling is configured; the ADR covers reading face at scale 1 but not HUD text faces. Confidence: medium on (1), (2); low on (3), which is not probed. (4) On Windows the main loop is driven from a timer during the modal edge-drag resize loop (recalled, not verified), which the step-11 2 s drag should cover. (5) Shader Baker only bakes for the drivers enabled in the export preset, so the preset must include Vulkan; it is not supported under Compatibility (recalled).
findings.amendment: Add a Gotchas list to Implementation Guidelines. Zoom cooldown: use delta divided by Engine.time_scale, or state that time_scale is always 1. Add a step-11 line for HUD text sharpness at H=3. Add a step-11 line for edge-drag cadence. Name the required drivers in the export preset checklist.

findings.text: canvas_transform is a Transform2D, which is float32 in the standard build. Integer-valued origins are exact only below 2^24 (16,777,216) base px. ADR-0005/0010 already list 'float32 canvas exactness' as an unverified assumption owned partly by ADR-0008. The camera solver holds float64 scalars, so the conversion to the float32 origin is the point where exactness is lost or kept. Confidence: medium (not probed here; Engine.is_double_precision() was not checked).
findings.amendment: State the exactness bound next to the camera write: pose_q is Vector2i, converted at the write, and body-frame coordinates are rebased so they stay inside the bound (the rebase mechanism already exists). Add a unit test at the bound. Resolve the ADR-0005/0010 'float32 canvas exactness' reference by citing this section.

The release build would then ship a different look with only a diagnostics-header line. Confidence: high that the keys exist and default to true; the silent fallback sequence itself is not probed.
findings.amendment: Add to the S5.1 table as required keys in project.godot: fallback_to_opengl3=false, and fallback_to_d3d12=false while Vulkan is the pin (fallback_to_vulkan=false if the D3D12 reversal is taken). A failed driver init then errors visibly instead of degrading silently. Make the release-build response to a method mismatch a visible fatal 'unsupported GPU' screen, or at least a user-facing notice, not a header log line.

findings.text: OQ-C and the 'probed 2026-10-28' claims. Windowed 4.7.2: a project with no driver key reports driver=vulkan / forward_plus. ProjectSettings default for rendering_device/driver.windows is vulkan, linuxbsd is vulkan, macos is metal. The reference's 'D3D12 is the Windows default since 4.6' is therefore not what a key-absent project gets; it is most plausibly a new-project-template value (UNVERIFIED, not probed). The ADR's effective-value assertion handles both cases and is the right approach. Also confirmed present with the stated defaults: display/window/hdr/request_hdr_output=false, per_pixel_transparency/allowed=false, use_debanding=false, hdr_2d=false, scale_mode=fractional, allow_hidpi=true, snap_controls_to_pixels=true, low_processor_mode=false, vsync_mode=1, default_texture_filter=1, snap_2d_*=false, default_clear_color=(0.3,0.3,0.3,1). The SubViewport/SubViewportContainer defaults I re-ran are plausible and match. One caveat: all of these headless probes ran under Compatibility, as the ADR itself says, and only the project-setting defaults are renderer-independent. Confidence: high.
findings.amendment: Edit OQ-C to record that a project with no key gets vulkan on 4.7.2 (windowed probe) and that the D3D12 default is probably a template write. Suggest correcting docs/engine-reference/godot/modules/rendering.md and breaking-changes.md accordingly. Do not claim more than this without opening the project-creation flow.

findings.text: Two CanvasLayers at the same layer index: probed, the later sibling (green) draws over the earlier (red). This is consistent with the engine passing the node's sibling index as the sublayer stacking key. This resolves the 'tree order UNVERIFIED' part of S2.5/OQ-G for siblings under one parent. It is fragile to reparenting or reordering. Confidence: high for same-parent siblings; not tested across different parents.
findings.amendment: Cheapest and robust: give MenuReadingLayer its own index (pixel face 3, reading face 4, debug 5) and drop the shared-index dependency. If the shared index is kept, record the sibling-index tie-break as probed, require both layers under PipelineRoot in a fixed order, and add a boot-walk assertion on their get_index() order.

findings.text: Answers to ADR-0009 questions about the snap flags and units under pass B (probed on a 600x12 viewport, override 200x4, stretch true, snap_2d_transforms_to_pixel=true). canvas_transform is in override (base-pixel) units: an x offset of -5 moved content by 15 screen px. Snapping happens in base-pixel space: a node at 10.4 with offset -5 gives 5.4, which snaps to 5, drawn at screen x=15. So the 'belt and braces' flags do snap to base pixels, not screen pixels, under pass B. They round to nearest rather than floor, which does not matter when placement is integer. Confidence: medium (single probe, Forward+).
findings.amendment: Record the result in S2.2/S4 and tell ADR-0009 that the snap flags snap to base px in both passes. Keep 'nothing relies on them'. Note that pose_q and parallax offsets must still be written as integer-valued Vector2 so rounding versus floor never differs.

findings.text: OQ-B/Verification (6), partial: a SubViewportContainer with stretch=false, scale=(3,3) and texture_filter=NEAREST drew an 8x4 viewport as exactly 24x12 screen px with a flat fill, with no bleed on either side and exact colour (SDR viewport). The width was exactly 24 px (x=700..723). Not tested: textured or non-flat content, fractional container position, Compatibility, pass B, release export. Confidence: medium for pass A flat content only.
findings.amendment: Keep step 11, but narrow it to the untested combinations: a textured sheet, a one-pixel checker, pass B, and an odd window size. Record the flat-fill probe as already passing.

findings.text: Draw-call accounting (OQ-F), probed in Forward+ and Compatibility. Viewport.get_render_info(RENDER_INFO_TYPE_CANVAS, RENDER_INFO_DRAW_CALLS_IN_FRAME) works per viewport. A root with only three SubViewportContainers reported 3 canvas draw calls, so the container composite IS counted on the root (one call per container). The sub-viewport's own count was separate (1 for one ColorRect). The signature and enum names in S7 are correct. So D_root closed is 63, not 62, in the ADR's own arithmetic (60 + 1 hold + 1 filter + 1 composite), and the chart-open figure 92 rises to 93 unless D_L3 is lowered. Confidence: medium-high (small scene).
findings.amendment: Add an explicit 'container composite' row (1 call, root) to S7.1 and fix D_root (63 and 93, or re-derive the caps). Resolve OQ-F from this probe and re-run in the release export. Add a note that DRAW_CALLS_IN_FRAME is read after the frame, so it lags one frame when read in _process.

findings.text: API, compile and typing review found nothing that fails on 4.7.2. I wrote the Key Interfaces into a scratch project and compiled them headless: RenderLayout (static derive returning its own class, Vector2i/PackedInt32Array), PipelineRoot read-only properties with get-only accessors (layout, present_time), and StartupCheck.run returning Array[StartupFinding]. All 24 class_names in the ADR (DisplaySettings, RenderLayout, ViewportWiring, PipelineRoot, CameraSolver, Pose, SolverInput and so on) do not collide with engine classes (ClassDB.class_exists false for all). layout, version and present_time are not Node or Object properties or methods. There is no const of a constructed object (the constants are ints, floats or a table). The 4.7 typed-return override rule is not triggered, since the only override is _process (void). The packed-array setter change (4.7) is not touched. Minor issues: (a) offered_h: PackedInt32Array is passed by reference in a 'pure/immutable' derive. A caller that mutates it after the call, or a layout that keeps it, changes the result. (b) S3.3 gives world_to_hud(body_pos) with one argument while Key Interfaces gives (body_pos, pose_q). (c) 'immutable value' RenderLayout declares a mutable var version. (d) With ADR-0010's all-warnings-as-errors, RenderConfigReader must cast every ProjectSettings.get_setting() Variant, because inferred or unsafe declarations are errors. Confidence: high for compile result; medium for (d).
findings.amendment: Copy or duplicate() offered_h on entry, or take Array[int]. Make the world_to_hud signature one way (the two-argument form) in S3.3. Move version out of the value (PipelineRoot holds the counter) or drop the 'immutable' claim. Add a one-line note that the reader uses explicit typed casts.

findings.text: S4 says RENDER_MODE is 'a single build constant' read only by ViewportWiring, but Validation Criteria and Equivalence require 'a test constructs both wirings from the same input trace'. A GDScript const cannot be varied in a test.
findings.amendment: Make the mode a constructor argument of ViewportWiring (enum Mode {A, B}); the composition root passes a default from one const or feature tag. The equivalence test then constructs both. Keep the 'only ViewportWiring branches on it' lint.

findings.text: Engine gotchas the draft does not mention. (1) The zoom cooldown uses _process delta, which is scaled by Engine.time_scale; the ADR says 'engine process time'. ADR-0001 leaves time_scale scaling UNVERIFIED, so the cooldown is only 'wall-clock' if time_scale stays 1. (2) A Control with a non-Control parent (WorldContainer under a plain Node) lays out against the window, and the container's Control.size is only refreshed from the viewport's minimum size at the next deferred update. The probe shows drawing is unaffected with stretch=false, but any code that reads WorldContainer.size or mouse rects right after a resize sees stale values; only scale and position should be read. (3) Dynamic-font Labels and RichText under CanvasLayer.scale=H are rasterised at font size and then upscaled (blurry, not pixel-snapped) unless a bitmap face or font oversampling is configured; the ADR covers reading face at scale 1 but not HUD text faces. Confidence: medium on (1), (2); low on (3), which is not probed. (4) On Windows the main loop is driven from a timer during the modal edge-drag resize loop (recalled, not verified), which the step-11 2 s drag should cover. (5) Shader Baker only bakes for the drivers enabled in the export preset, so the preset must include Vulkan; it is not supported under Compatibility (recalled).
findings.amendment: Add a Gotchas list to Implementation Guidelines. Zoom cooldown: use delta divided by Engine.time_scale, or state that time_scale is always 1. Add a step-11 line for HUD text sharpness at H=3. Add a step-11 line for edge-drag cadence. Name the required drivers in the export preset checklist.

findings.text: canvas_transform is a Transform2D, which is float32 in the standard build. Integer-valued origins are exact only below 2^24 (16,777,216) base px. ADR-0005/0010 already list 'float32 canvas exactness' as an unverified assumption owned partly by ADR-0008. The camera solver holds float64 scalars, so the conversion to the float32 origin is the point where exactness is lost or kept. Confidence: medium (not probed here; Engine.is_double_precision() was not checked).
findings.amendment: State the exactness bound next to the camera write: pose_q is Vector2i, converted at the write, and body-frame coordinates are rebased so they stay inside the bound (the rebase mechanism already exists). Add a unit test at the bound. Resolve the ADR-0005/0010 'float32 canvas exactness' reference by citing this section.

cross_adr.text: Camera solve location conflict (ADR-0009 OQ-J). ADR-0008 solves in frame_pre_draw. ADR-0009 solves at CAMERA_SOLVE stage 1 in the driver's _process because the HUD (stage 5) needs world_to_hud. The 4.7.2 probe shows frame_pre_draw fires after all _process, so a solve there is invisible to _process readers for a frame (see E2). ADR-0009's position is the one that works on this engine.
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0008 S6.1/S6.2/S7.3 and the diagram: move CameraSolver.solve into the CAMERA_SOLVE stage. The frame_pre_draw handler only writes canvas_transform and parallax offsets from the solved pose. ADR-0009 needs no change beyond citing the probed ordering.

cross_adr.text: Presenter execution model and priority label. ADR-0008 (S6.2 scope edge and diagram) says subscribers draw from their own _process at priority 0. ADR-0009 says presenters define no _process and a single PresentationHost, which may be the Pipeline root, calls a PresentationDriver at ProcessPriority.PRESENTATION (OQ-L). PipelineRoot at the same priority as subscribers would tie on tree order, which ADR-0001 refuses to rely on.
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0008 declares PipelineRoot to be the PresentationHost (ADR-0009 asks ADR-0008 to decide). Its single _process first does present_time, the zoom cooldown and the RESCALING re-derive, then calls driver.frame(). Replace the literal '0' in the diagram with ProcessPriority.PRESENTATION. No new ADR-0001 constant is needed.

cross_adr.text: OQ-D asks ADR-0001 for an additive PRESENTATION_LATE constant as the fallback camera-write point. With frame_pre_draw probed as working (E3) and the solve moved (X1), the request is unnecessary.
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0008 withdraws OQ-D. ADR-0001 stays at three constants. Re-check in the release-export probe.

cross_adr.text: ADR-0009 (snap-flag lines near 264 and 377) defers 'what the snap flags snap to under the SubViewport variants' to ADR-0008. Probe: they snap to base-pixel space under pass B, and canvas_transform is in base-pixel units (E8).
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0008 records the probe result in S2.2/S4. ADR-0009 cites it and may drop the 'unknown' wording.

cross_adr.text: ADR-0010 PRJ-02 delegates the stretch pins to ADR-0008, but ADR-0008 S5.1 adds more required project.godot keys: scale_mode=integer, window overrides, default_texture_filter=0, snap_2d_*, clear colour, and (per E5) the fallback_to_* keys. ADR-0010's warnings-as-errors policy also forces typed casts on ProjectSettings reads in RenderConfigReader.
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0010 PRJ-02 references ADR-0008 S5.1 as the normative key list (including the fallback_to_* keys once added). The RenderConfigReader lint exemption or cast pattern is stated once there.

cross_adr.text: ADR-0005 and ADR-0010 both cite 'float32 canvas exactness' as an assumption owned partly by ADR-0008, which ADR-0008 does not address (E14).
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0008 adds the 2^24 integer-exactness bound and the Vector2i-to-float32 conversion point at the canvas_transform write; ADR-0005/0010 then cite it.
